salient_findings: 1-year history of slow but progressive swelling near the gluteal cleft
4 × 4 cm area of swelling with mild blanching erythema
No fluid obtained on percutaneous aspiration
Complex and septated 6 × 4 × 4 cm mass excised from subcutaneous tissue
key_facts: 32-year-old woman
1-year history of swelling
Swelling located near the gluteal cleft
No fevers, chills, pain, drainage, bleeding, or rectal bleeding
Mild blanching erythema of the overlying skin
No fluctuance, purulence, or visible pilonidal pits
Percutaneous aspiration performed with no fluid obtained
Surgical excision of a complex and septated mass
Mass was adherent to subcutaneous fat but did not involve the coccyx or anal sphincter

shortlist.label: Epidermoid cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of a slow-growing, painless mass near the gluteal cleft with overlying skin erythema is consistent with an epidermoid cyst

shortlist.label: Pilonidal sinus
shortlist.why_kept: Location near the gluteal cleft and history of swelling are consistent with a pilonidal sinus, although the absence of fluctuance or purulence makes this less likely

shortlist.label: Dermoid cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to epidermoid cysts, dermoid cysts can present as slow-growing, painless masses, and the location near the gluteal cleft is plausible

shortlist.label: Lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: The mass was described as being adherent to subcutaneous fat, which could be consistent with a lipoma, although the complex and septated nature of the mass is less typical

shortlist.label: Soft tissue sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely, the complex and septated nature of the mass, as well as its size, could be concerning for a soft tissue sarcoma, and this diagnosis should be considered in the differential

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of a slow-growing, painless swelling near the gluteal cleft, along with the surgical excision of a complex and septated mass in the subcutaneous tissue, is most consistent with an epidermoid cyst. The lack of fluid on percutaneous aspiration and the absence of signs of infection also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Pilonidal sinus
rejected.why: The absence of visible pilonidal pits and the lack of drainage or purulence make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Dermoid cyst
rejected.why: While possible, dermoid cysts are less common than epidermoid cysts and often present with more complex symptoms or signs of infection.

rejected.label: Lipoma
rejected.why: The description of the mass as complex and septated is not typical of a lipoma, which is usually a simple, fatty tumor.

rejected.label: Soft tissue sarcoma
rejected.why: The slow growth and lack of systemic symptoms make a soft tissue sarcoma less likely, although pathology results would be necessary to rule out this diagnosis completely.
